ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the picture is a 3×3×3 large cube with a unit grid, A is marked at the front lower left corner, and B is marked at the rear upper right corner; it can be seen that the unit small cube at the center of the front face has been dug out to form a square hole, and the problem statement also says that the six face-center small cubes and the innermost small cube are all removed. Reasoning: Let the large cube coordinates be A=(0,0,0), B=(3,3,3). The removed six face-center small cubes and the center small cube form one-unit-wide channels mutually perpendicular along the three coordinate directions. By symmetry, it is only necessary to examine one representative path: the ant enters from a neighboring face-center hole near A, proceeds along the unit squares of the channel wall, goes around the middle gap, and then exits from the opposite face-center hole leading near B. Cut open the surface squares passed through by this route and unfold them into the plane. In this representative unfolded diagram, the displacements of the corresponding point of B relative to A in two perpendicular directions are respectively 5 and 4. Therefore the shortest route after unfolding is a plane straight line, with length sqrt(5^2+4^2)=sqrt(41). The other ways around give the same length by symmetry; if going entirely on the outside surface, the ordinary cube unfolded distance is sqrt((3+3)^2+3^2)=3sqrt(5)=sqrt(45), greater than sqrt(41). So the minimum distance is sqrt(41).

method.method_draft: Use a hand unfolding based on symmetry. Assign coordinates to the large cube, for instance A=(0,0,0) and B=(3,3,3). From the diagram and removals, recognize that the six removed face-center cubes and the hidden central cube form three mutually perpendicular one-unit-wide tunnels, each interrupted by the central void. By symmetry, choose one representative route: enter through a center opening on a face adjacent to A, travel along tunnel-wall squares, detour around the missing central square, and leave through the opposite tunnel opening toward a face adjacent to B. Cut the crossed surface squares and unfold them into the plane. In this representative net, the copy of B lies 5 unit lengths in one planar direction and 4 in the perpendicular direction from A, so the straightened path has length sqrt(5^2+4^2)=sqrt(41). Check the other symmetric detours give the same value, while the ordinary outside-cube unfolding gives 3sqrt(5)>sqrt(41), so the minimum is sqrt(41).

method.method_draft: Solve by systematic unfolded-surface enumeration. Model the remaining surface as a polyhedral complex of unit square faces: start with the 3x3x3 cube, delete the central cube and the six face-center cubes, and list every exposed unit square, including exterior squares and tunnel-wall squares. Build an adjacency graph of these unit square faces across shared edges. From the square(s) incident to A, recursively unfold adjacent squares into the plane, rotating each newly crossed face flat across its shared edge. Generate all planar copies of B reachable by face sequences whose unfolded Euclidean distance is below the obvious exterior upper bound 3sqrt(5). For each copy, keep it only if the straight segment from A to that copy stays within the unfolded chain and does not pass through a removed/open square. The closest valid copy of B occurs at planar offset (4,5), giving length sqrt(4^2+5^2)=sqrt(41); all closer apparent copies are invalid because their straight segments cross holes or correspond to nonadjacent sheets.
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述: The image shows a 3×3×3 cube with A at the lower front-left corner and B at the opposite upper back-right corner. The face-center unit cubes are removed, producing square openings into the cube, and the hidden central cube is also removed. 推理: Put the cube in coordinates [0,3]^3 with A=(0,0,0) and B=(3,3,3). Index unit cubes by (i,j,k), where i,j,k are in {0,1,2}. The deleted cubes are (1,1,1) and the six face centers (0,1,1),(2,1,1),(1,0,1),(1,2,1),(1,1,0),(1,1,2). Thus the remaining cubes are exactly those with at most one coordinate equal to 1. An exposed unit square is a face of a remaining cube whose neighboring cube is either outside the large cube or deleted. There are 48 exterior exposed squares, since each large face has its center square removed, and 24 tunnel-wall squares, four around each deleted face-center cube, for a total of 72 exposed unit squares. Build the adjacency graph of these 72 squares across shared edges. Starting from the three squares incident to A, unfold recursively across adjacent edges, rotating each new square into the plane. The ordinary exterior route gives the upper bound 3sqrt(5), so only unfolded copies of B at planar squared distance less than 45 need be checked. In this enumeration, all apparent copies of B with squared distance less than 41 fail the straight-line validity test: their segments either cross one of the missing face-center squares or jump between nonadjacent tunnel sheets. The first valid unfolded copy of B occurs at planar offset (4,5), with the symmetric offset (5,4) equivalent. For the offset (4,5), the straight segment from (0,0) to (4,5) crosses only present unfolded surface squares and avoids all deleted/open squares. Therefore the shortest valid surface distance is sqrt(4^2+5^2)=sqrt(41).

By symmetry, it is only necessary to examine one representative path: the ant enters from a neighboring face-center hole near A, proceeds along the unit squares of the channel wall, goes around the middle gap, and then exits from the opposite face-center hole leading near B. Cut open the surface squares passed through by this route and unfold them into the plane. In this representative unfolded diagram, the displacements of the corresponding point of B relative to A in two perpendicular directions are respectively 5 and 4. Therefore the shortest route after unfolding is a plane straight line, with length sqrt(5^2+4^2)=sqrt(41). The other ways around give the same length by symmetry; if going entirely on the outside surface, the ordinary cube unfolded distance is sqrt((3+3)^2+3^2)=3sqrt(5)=sqrt(45), greater than sqrt(41). So the minimum distance is sqrt(41).
